title: Cereal label comparison sheet
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y5 lesson 6 (Cereal label comparison sheet (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 6: Healthy eating and a balanced diet. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: The Eatwell Guide
points: Fruit and vegetables: about a third

bullets: Traffic lights: green low, amber medium, red high

blocks.h: Two cereal labels (made up), per 100 g

questions.q: Colour each sugar, fat and salt value green, amber or red using the traffic-light table.
questions.a: Honey Crunch: sugar 28 g red, fat 4.0 g amber, salt 0.6 g amber. Oat Bran Flakes: sugar 8 g amber, fat 3.5 g amber, salt 0.4 g amber.

questions.q: Which cereal is healthier? Give two reasons from the labels.
questions.a: Oat Bran Flakes: much less sugar (8 g, not 28 g), more fibre (11 g, not 3 g), and less salt and saturated fat.

keywords.def: something in food the body needs, such as protein or vitamins
the right amounts of each food group
information on packaging about what is in food

questions.q: 4 g sugar per 100 g: which colour?
Which nutrient helps growth and repair?

questions.a: It keeps the digestive system healthy.

questions.q: Core: Compare two cereal labels (pupil PDF): which is healthier and why?
questions.a: Cereal B: lower sugar and salt per 100 g.

questions.q: Extend: Plan a balanced day of meals using the Eatwell Guide.
questions.a: Fruit and veg at most meals, starchy foods, protein, water.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why 'low fat' does not always mean healthy.
questions.a: Some low-fat foods add sugar instead.

questions.q: A cereal has 30 g sugar per 100 g. Traffic light?
questions.a: C) Red. More than 22.5 g per 100 g is high (red).

questions.q: Protein is for... A) growth and repair B) only energy C) nothing
Big question: how do you check a 'healthy' claim?
questions.a: Read the label per 100 g and its traffic lights.
